notes: Delete of a stored fact. The Birth of Venus is stored by city name (w1) or through the Uffizi (housed_in, with the catalogued chain housed_in o located_in ⊑ located_in). q3 ('in the same city') is a join over named individuals; David in Florence, and in no other city, is its bridge (firm). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check.

queries.ask: uffizi : located_in some (City and inv(born_in) value dante)
venus : located_in some (City and inv(located_in) value david)

fol.notes: located_in is a relation (transitive in RELATIONS.md; only one step is needed here), housed_in a function (functional). The catalogued chain housed_in o located_in is the firm museum_chain rule, and 'a place lies in one city' is firm, as in the DL file. 'The same city' asks for a city both works are located in. The Uffizi, the works and the cities are an enumeration (unique names). Delete of a stored fact: w1 stores The Birth of Venus under Florence by name, w2 only through the Uffizi, whose city is deleted.

venus_uffizi.says: Botticelli's The Birth of Venus hangs in the Uffizi Gallery. (stored)

museum_chain.says: A work is located where the museum that holds it is located.
museum_chain.z3: ForAll([x, m, c], Implies(And(housed_in(x) == m, located_in(m, c)), located_in(x, c)))

one_city.says: A place lies in one city.
one_city.z3: ForAll([x, c, d], Implies(And(city(c), city(d), located_in(x, c), located_in(x, d)), c == d))

queries.ask: Exists(c, And(city(c), located_in(venus, c), located_in(david, c)))
